attributes.value: Cross-model pose agreement: DockQ scores are computed for the Fv-antigen interface of each model's predicted complex, and consensus is the stated number of models predicting the same pose above the stated DockQ threshold. The paper states the decision rule as "For any given pair, a prediction was considered successful if the binder demonstrated structural agreement amongst more models than its decoy". The pair is decided by which member has agreement among more models, not by an interface confidence score; ipSAE does not enter this endpoint.

attributes.source_locator: Section 3.3.1, sentences beginning "To test this, we calculated DockQ scores" and "For any given pair, a prediction was considered successful"
attributes.value: Cross-model pose agreement: DockQ scores are computed for the Fv-antigen interface of each model's predicted complex, and consensus is the stated number of models predicting the same pose above the stated DockQ threshold. The paper states the decision rule as "For any given pair, a prediction was considered successful if the binder demonstrated structural agreement amongst more models than its decoy". The pair is decided by which member has agreement among more models, not by an interface confidence score; ipSAE does not enter this endpoint.

name: POISK pair coverage under cross-model structural consensus: metric_implementation

limitations: The negatives are putative. 7,647 of the 11,247 are nearest-CDR matches from the Observed Antibody Space and 3,600 are germline-reverted with randomised CDR-H3 at 85% or more total identity; the paper states they have not been experimentally validated for lack of binding.
Binder labels come from an LLM extraction of patent text, audited by the same model and then on a 40-record manual sample.

Excluding antibodies within 95% identity of SAbDab reduces but does not establish absence from any model's training data; the Discussion says incomplete training-data disclosure prevents fully excluding overlap.
Discrimination does not establish where the antibody binds: the best engine contacts an annotated epitope residue in 62.8% of the 1,232 annotated records.
Neither the benchmark code nor a split manifest is offered for download; only the dataset, the folding artifacts and the ipSAE tool URL are.
Author-reported throughout, retrospective, and not reproduced by Rewire.

attributes.value: The benchmark subset keeps novel, human-targeting antibodies with explicitly defined antigen sequences. Records indicating conditional (for example pH-dependent) binding were excluded because folding models do not account for those conditions. Antigen length was restricted to 50 to 750 residues for computational feasibility, duplicates were removed, and Diamond BLASTP excluded antibodies sharing 95% or more identity with any SAbDab antibody, leaving 11,247 unique antibody-antigen sequence sets.

attributes.value: Putative non-binders were built by KA-Search against the Observed Antibody Space for the closest VH CDR match to each binder, paired with the original antigen. For the 32% of records with no close OAS match, germline-encoded regions were reverted to their inferred germline sequences and the CDR-H3 loops randomised by sampling from AbLang predictions while keeping total identity at 85% or above. The final benchmark holds 22,494 records with an equal split between binding and non-binding instances.

attributes.value: Patent epitope residue annotations could be mapped to the folded antigen construct for 1,232 binder records. Even the best-scoring model, Protenix-v2, placed the antibody in contact with the annotated epitope in only 62.8% of cases. The paper concludes that binding discrimination does not establish accurate epitope localization and that a confident prediction is not necessarily a correct one.

attributes.value: Among the 11,247 benchmark binders, all 11,247 (100.0%) carry explicit binding evidence and a concrete antigen sequence, 5,967 (53.1%) a reported binding-affinity value, 3,888 (34.6%) any epitope characterisation and 1,232 (11.0%) a residue-level epitope. Within the 3,888 epitope-characterised records, 1,003 are discontinuous or conformational, 826 linear, 501 functional or competitive and 1,558 not further specified.

attributes.value: Antibody chains were collected from GenBank (heavy, lambda and kappa, 70 to 1000 amino acids) and classified with ANARCI, giving 10,110 eligible US patents. Antigen identification, chain pairing and 36 further fields were extracted from the patent text with the Google Generative AI Python library and the Gemini 3 Pro model, with Pydantic schemas. Missing antigen sequences were looked up in UniProt by target identity and organism. Gemini also acted as auditor: fields it flagged as not explicitly mentioned were excluded, and records flagged for incorrect chain pairing were removed.

attributes.value: All six models used MSAs computed with ColabFold and no templates. The diffusion-based models generated one sample at each of five random seeds; AlphaFold-Multimer used its five parameter models. The highest confidence prediction was selected for analysis. Each of the 22,494 complexes was folded by all six engines with five predictions, giving 674,820 structure predictions and about 9,000 NVIDIA B200 GPU-hours; MSAs were computed once per unique sequence and excluded from the reported timings.

attributes.value: ipSAE was computed for the top-ranked structure of each record across all six models with a modified implementation of the ipSAE tool (https://github.com/DunbrackLab/IPSAE), using the predicted structures and their PAE matrices. The metric was computed asymmetrically with the paired antibody VH and VL concatenated as a single chain against the target (VH+VL to Target), with a PAE cutoff of 10 angstrom and a distance cutoff of 10 angstrom. The full-Fv ipSAE was selected as the primary evaluation metric for all subsequent analyses.

attributes.value: To test whether the engines simply prefer patent-derived sequences, 300 benchmark datapoints were sampled under a target-uniqueness constraint, balanced 150 germline-reverted and 150 OAS-matched, and their targets shuffled so that neither candidate binds the antigen it is folded against; the sampling was repeated under five seeds (42 to 46), giving 30,000 structure predictions and about 250 NVIDIA B200 GPU-hours. On the invalid triplets Protenix-v2 scored the patent-derived sequence higher in 50.3% of surviving pairs against 72.4% on the same pairs with their correct targets, and Boltz-2 52.5% against 55.4%.

The v1 PDF did not: three downloads on 2026-11-16 gave 3389c1bf6d3654c5b2151a07fcfcefc67cf6f36e5f0facfc03c33521d8b84491 twice and d699fd680e3b0097ca80130c288e8d872773dc1e523044f4605e06fc4f89d9bc once, none equal to the recorded artifact_sha256, because bioRxiv regenerates the container on request. A pdftotext -layout run (poppler 26.08.0) on all three downloads gave the same text layer, byte for byte the contents of the archived artifacts/biorxiv-v1-layout.txt.gz, SHA-256 e75c18130ca43770d2f0ed05ae96528759666c0e4fa08f7725f5a32b21187696, so the archive is provably derived from the pinned article and is the artifact this review verified values against. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly (36 in_cell, 36 in_row, 6 locator_not_parsed, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row) and wrote an identical value-check.tsv. All 78 results were then re-read by review/check_values_independent.py, written for this pass and importing nothing from extract/build_batch.py: it takes each table's column spans from the character offsets of the label text in that table's own printed header lines, assigns every numeric token on a body row to the column whose centre is nearest and rejects the row unless the token count matches the column count, the nearest column is the one in the token's own left-to-right position, and the runner-up column loses by at least three characters; it also checks that Table 1's sub-columns sit under their group labels and that Table 7's Coverage group does not reach the Ties column. Records are matched to cells through each result's source_locator text, not its ID. 72 results were checked in cell, including all 36 the repository parser could only place at row level, and the 6 prose values were checked against the sentence each locator names. Two negative controls confirmed the checker fails on a swapped pair of values and on a value shifted into a neighbouring column of the same row, which a row-level check passes. Independently of the script, all 42 printed cells of Tables 2 and 7 were transcribed by hand into review/manual-transcription.tsv and compared with the records, covering column assignment for every one of the 36 cells left unverified at extraction. attributes.value: Benchmark pairs were grouped by the publication date of the binder's source patent, one bucket before 2018 and six-month buckets to H1 2025, with bucket sizes from 305 to 3,229 pairs and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Accuracy does not systematically decline toward more recent patents: Protenix-v2 moves from 0.716 to 0.689 and IntelliFold v2 from 0.654 to 0.669. Splitting at each engine's stated PDB training cutoff, the largest pre-minus-post difference across all six engines is 1.8 percentage points (IntelliFold v2) and 0.6 points for both Protenix releases, against a spread between engines of more than ten points.

attributes.value: When both members of a pair fail to produce a confident interface, ipSAE returns exactly zero for both and the pair is undecidable; such pairs are scored at 0.5 rather than dropped. OpenFold3 leaves 37.9% of pairs undecidable and Protenix-v2 only 2.9%, so part of the gap between them at full coverage reflects how often each engine produces any interface prediction at all, not how well it ranks the ones it produces.

attributes.scope_note: 93,193 rows and 47 columns, each row carrying a distinct unique_record_id. The record states that version 1.1 corrects errors found in version 1.0.1 and adds the folding data for the paper's benchmark, and that those folding predictions were run against version 1.0.1 rather than against this release. The 93,193 rows are therefore not the manuscript's 89,074 extracted records and not the benchmark's 22,494 complexes. Relationship to version 1.0.1, after review: no link is recorded between the two dataset records. The releases do not hold the same data, so same_data_as, which states informational data reuse, does not apply: the Zenodo file lists give poisk_dataset.csv as 124,175,590 bytes with md5 1d663c6797f03466349c995b4e8a913a in version 1.0.1 and 234,128,089 bytes with md5 f0c1f098abf1756e4b9891aa4dc028ee here, and this record's own description says version 1.1 corrects errors found in version 1.0.1. supersedes is not recorded either, because version 1.0.1 is still the release the published folding predictions were run against and is what every evaluation in this batch pins. The two releases share poisk_all_models_folding_metrics.zip, md5 9b56b7095d32c3c2357aa6d4fa3369f8, which claim-v1-1-folding-metrics-files records, and claim-v1-1-folding-version carries the release's own statement about which version the predictions were run against.

The two Zenodo API responses, the explorer page and the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML all hashed to the values on their source records. The v1 PDF did not: three downloads on 2026-11-16 gave 3389c1bf6d3654c5b2151a07fcfcefc67cf6f36e5f0facfc03c33521d8b84491 twice and d699fd680e3b0097ca80130c288e8d872773dc1e523044f4605e06fc4f89d9bc once, none equal to the recorded artifact_sha256, because bioRxiv regenerates the container on request. A pdftotext -layout run (poppler 26.08.0) on all three downloads gave the same text layer, byte for byte the contents of the archived artifacts/biorxiv-v1-layout.txt.gz, SHA-256 e75c18130ca43770d2f0ed05ae96528759666c0e4fa08f7725f5a32b21187696, so the archive is provably derived from the pinned article and is the artifact this review verified values against. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly (36 in_cell, 36 in_row, 6 locator_not_parsed, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row) and wrote an identical value-check.tsv. All 78 results were then re-read by review/check_values_independent.py, written for this pass and importing nothing from extract/build_batch.py: it takes each table's column spans from the character offsets of the label text in that table's own printed header lines, assigns every numeric token on a body row to the column whose centre is nearest and rejects the row unless the token count matches the column count, the nearest column is the one in the token's own left-to-right position, and the runner-up column loses by at least three characters; it also checks that Table 1's sub-columns sit under their group labels and that Table 7's Coverage group does not reach the Ties column. Records are matched to cells through each result's source_locator text, not its ID. 72 results were checked in cell, including all 36 the repository parser could only place at row level, and the 6 prose values were checked against the sentence each locator names. Two negative controls confirmed the checker fails on a swapped pair of values and on a value shifted into a neighbouring column of the same row, which a row-level check passes. Independently of the script, all 42 printed cells of Tables 2 and 7 were transcribed by hand into review/manual-transcription.tsv and compared with the records, covering column assignment for every one of the 36 cells left unverified at extraction. Version 2 of the preprint, posted 2026-11-14, was retrieved (PDF SHA-256 aeaec593d7aa2d42382a49bd6fadbbccabaa6c084843ea1c7f0c91097dedb0c2, text layer 82a99bc2e061b7247cf65f7bc9450924b7af5be7ab3ef283d2284ba787ea629c): every numeric token in it is identical to v1's apart from an added author affiliation and the two Zenodo record identifiers, so no stored value changes and the batch stays pinned to v1. The v1 PDF did not: three downloads on 2026-11-16 gave 3389c1bf6d3654c5b2151a07fcfcefc67cf6f36e5f0facfc03c33521d8b84491 twice and d699fd680e3b0097ca80130c288e8d872773dc1e523044f4605e06fc4f89d9bc once, none equal to the recorded artifact_sha256, because bioRxiv regenerates the container on request. A pdftotext -layout run (poppler 26.08.0) on all three downloads gave the same text layer, byte for byte the contents of the archived artifacts/biorxiv-v1-layout.txt.gz, SHA-256 e75c18130ca43770d2f0ed05ae96528759666c0e4fa08f7725f5a32b21187696, so the archive is provably derived from the pinned article and is the artifact this review verified values against. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly (36 in_cell, 36 in_row, 6 locator_not_parsed, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row) and wrote an identical value-check.tsv. All 78 results were then re-read by review/check_values_independent.py, written for this pass and importing nothing from extract/build_batch.py: it takes each table's column spans from the character offsets of the label text in that table's own printed header lines, assigns every numeric token on a body row to the column whose centre is nearest and rejects the row unless the token count matches the column count, the nearest column is the one in the token's own left-to-right position, and the runner-up column loses by at least three characters; it also checks that Table 1's sub-columns sit under their group labels and that Table 7's Coverage group does not reach the Ties column. Records are matched to cells through each result's source_locator text, not its ID. 72 results were checked in cell, including all 36 the repository parser could only place at row level, and the 6 prose values were checked against the sentence each locator names. Two negative controls confirmed the checker fails on a swapped pair of values and on a value shifted into a neighbouring column of the same row, which a row-level check passes. Independently of the script, all 42 printed cells of Tables 2 and 7 were transcribed by hand into review/manual-transcription.tsv and compared with the records, covering column assignment for every one of the 36 cells left unverified at extraction. Version 2 of the preprint, posted 2026-11-14, was retrieved (PDF SHA-256 aeaec593d7aa2d42382a49bd6fadbbccabaa6c084843ea1c7f0c91097dedb0c2, text layer 82a99bc2e061b7247cf65f7bc9450924b7af5be7ab3ef283d2284ba787ea629c): every numeric token in it is identical to v1's apart from an added author affiliation and the two Zenodo record identifiers, so no stored value changes and the batch stays pinned to v1. The 40 descriptive claims were read against the pinned PDF text layer, both Zenodo API responses and the explorer page.

review.method_note: Independent review pass. All five pinned artifacts were re-retrieved. The two Zenodo API responses, the explorer page and the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML all hashed to the values on their source records. The v1 PDF did not: three downloads on 2026-11-16 gave 3389c1bf6d3654c5b2151a07fcfcefc67cf6f36e5f0facfc03c33521d8b84491 twice and d699fd680e3b0097ca80130c288e8d872773dc1e523044f4605e06fc4f89d9bc once, none equal to the recorded artifact_sha256, because bioRxiv regenerates the container on request. A pdftotext -layout run (poppler 26.08.0) on all three downloads gave the same text layer, byte for byte the contents of the archived artifacts/biorxiv-v1-layout.txt.gz, SHA-256 e75c18130ca43770d2f0ed05ae96528759666c0e4fa08f7725f5a32b21187696, so the archive is provably derived from the pinned article and is the artifact this review verified values against. npm run batch -- check-values reproduced the extractor's figures exactly (36 in_cell, 36 in_row, 6 locator_not_parsed, no wrong_column and no overclaimed_in_row) and wrote an identical value-check.tsv. All 78 results were then re-read by review/check_values_independent.py, written for this pass and importing nothing from extract/build_batch.py: it takes each table's column spans from the character offsets of the label text in that table's own printed header lines, assigns every numeric token on a body row to the column whose centre is nearest and rejects the row unless the token count matches the column count, the nearest column is the one in the token's own left-to-right position, and the runner-up column loses by at least three characters; it also checks that Table 1's sub-columns sit under their group labels and that Table 7's Coverage group does not reach the Ties column. Records are matched to cells through each result's source_locator text, not its ID. 72 results were checked in cell, including all 36 the repository parser could only place at row level, and the 6 prose values were checked against the sentence each locator names. Two negative controls confirmed the checker fails on a swapped pair of values and on a value shifted into a neighbouring column of the same row, which a row-level check passes. Independently of the script, all 42 printed cells of Tables 2 and 7 were transcribed by hand into review/manual-transcription.tsv and compared with the records, covering column assignment for every one of the 36 cells left unverified at extraction. Version 2 of the preprint, posted 2026-11-14, was retrieved (PDF SHA-256 aeaec593d7aa2d42382a49bd6fadbbccabaa6c084843ea1c7f0c91097dedb0c2, text layer 82a99bc2e061b7247cf65f7bc9450924b7af5be7ab3ef283d2284ba787ea629c): every numeric token in it is identical to v1's apart from an added author affiliation and the two Zenodo record identifiers, so no stored value changes and the batch stays pinned to v1. The 40 descriptive claims were read against the pinned PDF text layer, both Zenodo API responses and the explorer page.

The two Zenodo API responses, the explorer page and the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML all hashed to the values on their source records. All 78 results were then re-read by review/check_values_independent.py, written for this pass and importing nothing from extract/build_batch.py: it takes each table's column spans from the character offsets of the label text in that table's own printed header lines, assigns every numeric token on a body row to the column whose centre is nearest and rejects the row unless the token count matches the column count, the nearest column is the one in the token's own left-to-right position, and the runner-up column loses by at least three characters; it also checks that Table 1's sub-columns sit under their group labels and that Table 7's Coverage group does not reach the Ties column. Records are matched to cells through each result's source_locator text, not its ID. 72 results were checked in cell, including all 36 the repository parser could only place at row level, and the 6 prose values were checked against the sentence each locator names. Two negative controls confirmed the checker fails on a swapped pair of values and on a value shifted into a neighbouring column of the same row, which a row-level check passes. Independently of the script, all 42 printed cells of Tables 2 and 7 were transcribed by hand into review/manual-transcription.tsv and compared with the records, covering column assignment for every one of the 36 cells left unverified at extraction.
